title: Portfolio monitoring, rebalancing and performance reporting
objectives: Set a review cycle and rebalancing rule.
Report performance with XIRR against a fair benchmark.
body_md:
## Review routine

| Item | Practice |
|---|---|
| **Frequency** | At least yearly, plus on a life or market event |
| **Checks** | Goal progress, allocation drift, fund performance vs benchmark and peers, cost, risk profile change |
| **Output** | A written review with decisions and reasons |

## Rebalancing

- **Calendar:** reset to the target at a fixed date.
- **Band:** act when an asset class drifts beyond a limit (for example 5 percentage points).
- Prefer using **new money and redemptions** before selling, to limit tax and cost.

Example: target 60:40 equity:debt drifts to 70:30 after a rally. Redirect new investments to debt, or sell part of equity if the band is breached.

## Reporting performance

- Use **XIRR** for cash-flow-driven portfolios, **CAGR** for a single lump sum.
- Compare with the **right benchmark** (TRI, matching the mandate).
- Show returns **net of fees and costs**, over several periods.
- Report risk too: volatility and drawdown.

## Behaviour

Frequent reviews should not turn into frequent changes. Change the plan when the **goal or circumstances change**, not because last quarter was poor.

> **Exam tip:** Use XIRR for periodic investments; rebalance by rule, not by mood.
example: A 60:40 plan drifts to 70:30. At a 5-point band the adviser redirects new money to debt and records the reason.
say: We review once a year against your goals, not against last month.
I rebalance by rule, so emotion does not decide.
never: Switch funds whenever a competitor tops the table.
Compare an equity fund with a fixed deposit rate only.
